attacks.claim: The plan moves embeddings and chunks derived from customer documents into Nimbus Vector Store, which is provisioned in us-east-2. This violates the DPA constraint that all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) be processed and stored in the EU. EU regions are only a roadmap item with no date.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." Week 2: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store"

attacks.claim: Week 3 releases the GPU reservation and deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters before cutover (week 4) and before any regression eval. This destroys the only rollback path and the fine-tuned assets. Recreating the adapters means retraining, and the reservation may not be recoverable.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: The agreed release gate is the 4,100-case regression suite for any model change. The plan defers it until after cutover, justified by a 25-question blind preference test, which is far too small to show parity. The test also does not cover the LoRA-to-system-prompt change, and the prompts were only drafted in week 1. It measures preference, not correctness on legal QA.
attacks.evidence: "This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: All tenants are cut over at once in week 4, with no canary, no staged rollout and no fallback. pgvector is removed in week 5, and the self-hosted stack is already gone. A failure or regression would hit every law-firm customer, and there is no stated recovery path. Dual-write covers only new documents, and there is no consistency check against the old index.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus"; "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool"

attacks.claim: The plan makes one vendor responsible for generation, embeddings and the vector store, drops the self-hosted fine-tuned model, and deletes the weights. The vector store is a preview-stage product. Exit cost is very high: re-embedding 41M chunks, rebuilding the adapters, and re-provisioning the GPUs. The plan has no exit strategy.
attacks.evidence: "Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector"; "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters"

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation rests on a preview-stage managed product, using per-tenant collections and tenant-scoped keys. The plan has no isolation testing, and the 'mirrors today's' claim is unsupported. Per-tenant keys at scale add key-management load that is not covered by the 30-day rotation plan. Privileged document content also goes to a third party.
attacks.evidence: "one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key, mirroring today's per-tenant pgvector schemas"

attacks.claim: The 1,536-dim Nimbus embeddings replace the current embeddings, so the full corpus must be re-embedded. Retrieval quality will change, and the plan has no retrieval-quality eval (recall@k) for the change. The 200k-context claim is also used as a benefit, but nothing tests answer quality at that length.
attacks.evidence: "Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims)"; "Nimbus Atlas-L supports 200k context natively"

attacks.claim: The cost table covers only a steady state and leaves out the one-time re-embedding of 41M chunks, the dual-write period and the cost of a long-context, per-token pricing model. The generation figure ($7,900) is an unsupported estimate with no basis shown. Per-token cost could grow if the 200k context is used. Savings are reported as sure, but the line items are not.

The rate-limit headroom is checked only against average peak (40 req/s vs 120). Long-context requests and the use of tokens-per-minute limits are not considered. Re-embedding 41M chunks in one week may hit embedding quotas, and no throughput math is given.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s"; "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks)"

attacks.claim: Privileged legal documents and their derived embeddings would be sent to an external processor, and a US-hosted store would hold them. The plan has no DPA/subprocessor update, no customer notification and no DPIA. The ZDR addendum covers only the inference API, not Vector Store, which holds persistent data.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)" (applies to generation; Vector Store retention not addressed)
